title: Exam review: Module 5 · infections, infestations, photodermatoses & travel
summary: All 30 questions from the Module 5 end-of-module exam, with the recommended UK answer, why the distractors are wrong and links to the matching condition pages. Themes: Reiter’s vs Behçet’s, Lyme management, the Kaposi sarcoma virus, pyoderma gangrenosum.

article.title: About this review
blocks: Revision key for the DermUSW end-of-module exam for Module 5 (Jun 2024): 30 single-best-answer questions. **Saved** is the answer ticked before submission (not a graded course key). **Recommended** is the teaching answer on current UK guidance (NICE / CKS, BNF, BAD, BASHH, Resuscitation Council UK, UKHSA).

list: ✗ the saved answer is probably wrong

Each question links to the condition page that covers the topic, where one exists.

head: Q
Topic
Saved
Recommended
Why, and why the distractors are wrong
Read more
rows: Itchy papular rash on legs/soles after swimming in the Nile, feverish
Freshwater exposure in Egypt or Sudan. Refer to infectious diseases (serology from 6–12 weeks; praziquantel). Dengue has no freshwater link. Scabies is not this acute
Hand blisters and fragility, **naproxen**, normal porphyrins
Looks like PCT, but porphyrins are normal and there is an NSAID. Stop naproxen
Crab lice in pubic hair and eyelashes
*Pediculus humanus* is head/body lice. Offer a **full STI screen** (BASHH)
Swimmer, malodorous white plantar skin with pits
Hyperhidrosis, occlusion. Topical clindamycin/erythromycin/fusidic acid or BPO, plus aluminium chloride. Erythrasma (coral-red under Wood's lamp) is in the flexures
Recurrent grouped vesicles on the lip after a cold
Prodrome, recurrence at the same site. Angular cheilitis is fissuring at the angles of the mouth
Green-black hallux nail, onycholysis, KOH-negative, failed terbinafine

Pyocyanin pigment. Keep the nail dry, trim the onycholytic nail, topical antiseptic (e.g. dilute vinegar/chlorhexidine soaks) ± topical antibiotic. **Exclude subungual melanoma if the colour is black or brown**
14-year-old, palpable purpura on legs, arthralgia, abdominal pain after a sore throat, normal platelets

Palpable purpura with a normal platelet count. **Check urine and BP** for nephritis, with follow-up dipsticks. ITP has low platelets. Meningococcaemia is an unwell child with non-palpable purpura (emergency)
**Occlusive white soft paraffin (petroleum jelly) to the lashes twice daily for ~8–10 days** (BASHH)
Insecticides are not for use near the eye. Lindane is withdrawn. Tea tree oil irritates
Exaggerated sunburn minutes after sun exposure, recently started furosemide
Furosemide (and amlodipine less so) are photosensitisers. Medication review
3-month-old, napkin rash with satellite lesions despite zinc oxide
**Topical imidazole (miconazole or clotrimazole) for 7–14 days**, ± 1% HC if inflamed
Satellite papules = *Candida*. Neomycin/betamethasone is too potent and sensitising for an infant. Oral nystatin only if there is oral thrush
UVA and visible light don't convert 7-dehydrocholesterol. Supplement vitamin D (10 micrograms/day) in sun-avoiders and NMSC patients
Painless ulcer with raised edge, Colombian Amazon
**Cutaneous leishmaniasis** (New World, so a **mucosal** risk with *L. braziliensis*)
Refer to the HTD (London) or the Liverpool tropical service. Sporotrichosis spreads along lymphatics
Serpiginous itchy track on the foot after a Caribbean beach

**Topical thiabendazole is the best of the listed options**. UK practice is **oral ivermectin 200 micrograms/kg single dose (unlicensed) or albendazole 400 mg daily for 3 days** via the travel clinic or specialist
Hookworm CLM. Itraconazole, neomycin and clobetasol don't kill larvae. Topical thiabendazole 10–15% is effective but is a UK special
Painful rapidly enlarging undermined ulcer after minor trauma, Crohn's

**Pathergy**, violaceous undermined edge, IBD. Don't debride. Same-week dermatology; potent topical steroid/tacrolimus or systemic therapy. PV gives erosions, not deep ulcers. Ecthyma gangrenosum is *Pseudomonas* sepsis in the neutropenic
Shallow medial gaiter ulcer, varicosities, better with elevation
Check ABPI before compression (NICE CKS / NWCSP). Arterial ulcers are punched out, lateral or on the foot, and painful on elevation
Post-sexual urethritis, then arthritis, conjunctivitis, **keratoderma blennorrhagicum** and **circinate balanitis**
"Can't see, can't pee, can't climb a tree" plus the classic skin signs. Refer to GUM (chlamydia/gonorrhoea) and rheumatology. Behçet's is **oral + genital ulcers** + uveitis (the answer to Q22)
Cellulitis, fever 38.3 °C, systemically well, uncontrolled T2DM and obesity

Class 2 = systemically unwell **or** well with comorbidity that may complicate or delay resolution (diabetes, obesity, PVD). Class 3 = significant systemic upset or limb-threatening. Class 1 = no toxicity or comorbidity
Sore (not itchy) lesions on back, arms and legs after a country hotel in a forest (image)
**Bed bugs (*Cimex*)** fits "hotel + back, arms and legs, multiple, often linear 'breakfast-lunch-dinner'". Tick bites are usually few, with an attached tick, in the flexures and waistband
Depends on the image. Multiple grouped or linear papules on the trunk and limbs favour bed bugs. A single erythema migrans favours ticks. Flea bites are on the lower legs
65-year-old, painful unilateral facial/ear/neck vesicles for 2 days
Aciclovir within 72 h (age >50). **Check eye (Hutchinson's sign)** and ear (Ramsay Hunt: facial palsy)

NICE **NG95**: EM is diagnostic, so **don't test**. Serology is often negative early. **Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily (or 200 mg once daily) for 21 days**; amoxicillin if doxycycline is unsuitable. Biopsy and waiting are wrong
Photo-distributed eczema sparing behind the ears and under the chin, abnormal UVB phototest
An older man with sharp demarcation and **reduced MED to UVB (± UVA/visible)**. PMLE is self-limiting and seasonal
Recurrent oral ulcers + genital ulcers + eye disease (uveitis) are the ISG criteria. RAS has no genital or eye involvement. SJS is acute and drug-related
Senegal migrant, foot swelling, nodules, draining sinuses, branched filaments
Triad of swelling, sinuses and grains. Actinomycetoma is treated with antibiotics (co-trimoxazole + amikacin). Eumycetoma needs antifungals + surgery
**Permethrin 5% plus oral ivermectin** (UKHSA 2023 care-home outbreak guidance)
Mass treatment of residents and staff on the same day. Ivermectin for crusted scabies and outbreaks. Lindane and malathion aren't recommended. Crotamiton is weak
HHV-8 causes KS, primary effusion lymphoma and multicentric Castleman disease. CMV causes retinitis/colitis. Treatment is effective ART ± chemotherapy
Painful dome-shaped swelling on the nape
A single follicle-centred abscess. Carbuncle is a multi-headed coalescence. Swab if recurrent (PVL). I&D if fluctuant
18-year-old, umbilicated papules on one side of the chest
Resolves over 6–18 months. Cryotherapy and curettage scar and hurt. **Consider sexual transmission or immunosuppression in adults with genital/extensive disease**
Guttate psoriasis has no herald patch. Secondary syphilis involves the palms and soles, so check serology if at risk
Linear blisters after gardening among hogweed, sun-exposed forearm
Furocoumarins (giant hogweed) + UVA, leading to linear blisters and then pigmentation lasting months. Cool compresses, potent TCS, sun protection
Thailand, high fever, retro-orbital headache, diffuse rash, prostration
Watch for warning signs of severe dengue. **Avoid NSAIDs/aspirin**. Use paracetamol. Exclude malaria the same day
